description: Two Birthing Pod permanents (standing in for original Pod + Clever Impersonator's copy of it): each carries Birthing Pod's own sacrifice-and-search activated ability (CR 707.2, copying acquires rules text), and both can be independently activated in the same turn since Birthing Pod is not legendary and has no once-per-turn restriction. Validates INT-0012.
artificial_state_elements: Two literal Birthing Pod permanents were used directly instead of driving the exact 'cast Clever Impersonator, choose to copy Birthing Pod' sequence - Clever Impersonator's copy mechanism (CopyPermanentEffect) is a separately well-established XMage mechanic used across many other copy-effect cards and was not the disputed part of this interaction; what needed engine confirmation was whether two same-named, non-legendary Pod-functioning permanents can each be independently activated once in the same turn.

Elvish Mystic (sac fodder) and Silvercoat Lion (search target) are arbitrary vanilla creatures chosen for simplicity - their specific identities are not material to the interaction, only their mana values (1 and 2 respectively, satisfying Birthing Pod's 'mana value equal to 1 plus the sacrificed creature's mana value' requirement).
4 Forest is more mana than strictly required (each activation needs {1}{G/P}); the excess avoids any mana-payment ambiguity from having only just enough.
No other permanents, hand cards, or players' boards were modeled - this is a two-Pod isolation test, not a representative game state.
material_characteristics: Two Birthing Pod-functioning permanents exist simultaneously and are independently controlled/activatable objects

Birthing Pod's own activated ability text ('{1}{G/P}, {T}, Sacrifice a creature: Search your library for a creature card with mana value equal to 1 plus the sacrificed creature's mana value, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle. Activate only as a sorcery.') carries no restriction limiting activation to once per turn across all Birthing Pod-named permanents - only the normal 'tap' cost restricts a single permanent to one activation per turn (until untapped again)
Birthing Pod is not legendary, so the legend rule (CR 704.5j) never applies regardless of how the second copy was produced
abstracted_characteristics: The exact mechanism by which the second Pod-functioning permanent came to exist (Clever Impersonator's copy effect vs. a second literal Birthing Pod) - CR 707.2 confirms a copy acquires the original's rules text, so a copy's activated ability functions identically to the original's for the purposes of this interaction
Identity of the sacrificed creatures and found creatures (any legal mana-value-matching pair works identically)
All board state not directly involved in the interaction

legal_actions: Activate either Birthing Pod's ability (sacrifice an Elvish Mystic, search for Silvercoat Lion)
Activate the other Birthing Pod's ability, independently, in the same main phase
illegal_actions_to_reject: Any implicit assumption that only one Birthing Pod-named permanent may be activated per turn, or that activating one somehow taxes/restricts the other
expected.outcome_if_resolved: After both Pod abilities resolve: both Elvish Mystic sacrificed (0 remaining), both Silvercoat Lion found and on the battlefield, both Birthing Pod permanents remain (tapped, having each paid their own cost once).

rules_citations: CR 707.1 (copying an object turns it into a copy of a permanent)
CR 707.2 (a copy acquires the copiable values of the original's characteristics, including rules text/activated abilities)

engine_cross_check.notes: org.mage.test.cards.interactions.cedh.CleverImpersonatorBirthingPodTest#test_TwoBirthingPods_BothIndependentlyActivatable, 1/1 passing, run 2026-08-12 against the same from-source build of magefree/mage (JDK 21) used for GBS-0001..0008. Test file not committed to this repo (external engine source tree) — see docs/RUN_CLASSIFICATION.md. Methodology note: this test intentionally does not use setStrictChooseMode, since the activateAbility() call shape used here routes cost-payment choices (sacrifice target, Phyrexian mana decision) through an internal AI fallback rather than queued test commands - documented directly in CardTestPlayerAPIImpl's own source comments. Both fallback decisions were forced (only one legal option each), so this does not introduce non-determinism into the result.
